note: Week of 2026-10-19 build. PRIOR WEEK (10/12-10/16) realized -1,481.79 (-1.98%), 5 of 11 names green: MPC +5.06% (+322.56), UNH +5.83% (+287.69), CCI +3.29%, VLO +2.53%, AMT +1.66%, AEM +0.27%. Losses: PLTR -11.01% (-713.62), PWR -10.49% (-666.72), CEG -8.96% (-587.40), AMZN -4.74%, HUM -4.33% - the AI-infrastructure/tech trade broke (Nasdaq -4.48%, SOX down 8 straight days, CoreWeave debt worries, Anthropic IPO valuation pushback). Exited all AI-power/tech (CEG, PWR, PLTR, AMZN), towers (CCI, AMT), HUM, refiners (MPC, VLO - VLO reports Thu, momentum stalled) and AEM. EARNINGS INSIDE THE WINDOW: NOC Tue 10/20 before the open (sized 5.7%) and LMT Thu 10/22 before the open (sized 6.0%). Other dated events: NFLX Tue pm; META, TSLA, IBM, TXN, LRCX, SAP Wed pm; ELV Wed am (managed-care read-through); RTX/GE Tue; jobless claims Thu; flash PMIs Fri. Fed in blackout ahead of the 10/27-28 FOMC. Macro: S&P 500 7,659 (-1.95% w/w, below its 50-day, first >1% daily drop in 55 sessions), Nasdaq 26,140 (-4.48%), Dow 52,001 (+0.67%); equal-weight S&P best week vs tech since 2009; 10-year 5.10% (-15 bp, best week since Feb); Brent $109.86 (highest since May 19), WTI ~$101; gold ~$4,181; Fear & Greed 30. Theme: follow the rotation - oil E&Ps at new highs (COP, EOG, XOM), defense into earnings (LMT, NOC), managed care/pharma (CI, UNH, LLY), defensives (WMT, SO, NI) and a blowout insurance beat (TRV). Zero tech, zero semis.

positions.name: ConocoPhillips
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $146.51, a new 52-week high and the high of the day, +9.3% on the week (from $134.10) - the best week of any large-cap E&P - on 7.8M shares Friday (1.3x the 2-week average). Brent settled Friday at $109.86 (+3.7%, highest close since May 19) and WTI ~$101 as Houthi missiles and drones hit Saudi airports and Aramco's Dhahran HQ and NATO weighed a response to Black Sea drone attacks. The equal-weight S&P had its best week vs tech since 2009 and energy led the rotation.
positions.risks: Crude is headline-driven: Iran has signaled openness to talks, and a visible de-escalation or Saudi success against Houthi launch sites would likely pull Brent back toward the low $100s (Brent opened Sunday night slightly lower at ~$109.1). Up ~70% off the November 2025 low. Q3 earnings are early November, outside the window.
positions.driver: Purest high-beta liquid oil exposure at a fresh 52-week high with oil at a 5-month high.

positions.name: EOG Resources
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $158.01, a new 52-week high, +3.5% on the day on 5.3M shares (1.85x the 2-week average) - the heaviest volume of the group - and +6.6% on the week, even as the stock went ex-dividend Friday ($1.02). Same oil catalyst as COP; EOG is the lowest-cost, highest-margin US shale producer and trades at ~12x earnings.
positions.risks: Same crude/de-escalation risk as COP (paired exposure). Q3 earnings early November, outside the window. Friday's volume spike could mark short-term exhaustion.
positions.driver: Volume-confirmed breakout to a new high - the strongest tape in shale.

positions.name: Exxon Mobil
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $178.98, a new 52-week/all-time high and the high of the day, +5.9% on the week (from $168.94) and its 3rd straight higher weekly close, on 13.2M shares (1.2x average). The steadiest large-cap way to own the $100+ oil regime; integrated downstream margins also benefit from the tight product market that drove refiners (MPC +5.1% w/w).
positions.risks: Same crude risk; lower beta than COP/EOG so it lags if oil spikes further. Q3 earnings ~10/30, outside the window. Energy is 26% of the book - the biggest single bet.
positions.driver: Mega-cap energy leader at all-time highs to anchor the oil trade.

positions.name: Lockheed Martin
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $552.09, +3.6% on the day and +8.3% on the week (from $509.59), at a 2-month high on 1.6M shares (1.44x average). Wednesday it jumped 3.6% on a Vertical Research Buy call and a $300M Texas missile-production expansion; Thursday/Friday extended on Saudi-Houthi escalation and NATO weighing a response to Black Sea drone attacks. Reports Q3 Thu 10/22 before the open (EPS est. $7.51) - the pre-earnings run is part of the trade.
positions.risks: Binary earnings Thursday - sized small (6.0%). Bernstein cut its PT on Congressional defense-funding worries. Still 20% below the $692 March high (F-35/classified-program charges were the 2026 overhang).
positions.driver: Defense momentum leader running into its own catalyst inside the window.

positions.name: Northrop Grumman
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $519.86, +4.0% on the day and +8.1% on the week (from $480.72), and +10.6% off its 10/2 52-week low ($470.06) - a sharp reversal on above-average volume (1.3M vs 0.99M). Same geopolitical bid as LMT. Reports Q3 Tue 10/20 before the open (EPS est. $7.19) - the first big defense print, which sets the tone for RTX (Tue) and LMT (Thu).
positions.risks: Binary earnings Tuesday - sized smallest (5.7%). Still 33% below the $774 March high: B-21 cost issues and a weak 2026 guide were the reasons for the selloff; a bad print could undo the bounce quickly.
positions.driver: Oversold defense prime reversing hard into earnings - asymmetric if the print is clean.

positions.name: Cigna Group
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $302.30, +7.0% on the week (from $282.43), five higher closes in six sessions and within 3% of its $311.34 52-week high. Piper Sandler lifted its PT to $370 from $346 after Cigna raised its 2026 outlook; the managed-care group re-rated after UNH's Q3 beat (10/13). CI has the least Medicare Advantage exposure of the big four, so it carries the lowest 2027-rate risk, at ~12.5x earnings.
positions.risks: Reports Q3 ~10/30, outside the window. ELV (Wed 10/21) and MOH (Wed pm) prints this week can move the group either way. PBM policy (drug-pricing rules) is a standing headline risk for Evernorth.
positions.driver: Cleanest managed-care chart, an upgrade-driven PT hike, and no MA overhang.

positions.name: UnitedHealth Group
positions.catalyst: Re-bought after last week's +5.83% gain; closed Friday 10/16 at $401.43, +5.8% on the week. Q3 beat on Tue 10/13 (stock spiked to $399.88 at the open, faded, then rallied Wed-Thu to a $414.12 high Thursday on 10.2M shares). Above $400 for the first time since August, with the 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings and a cleaner cost-trend print behind it.
positions.risks: Friday reversed from $412 to $401 (-1.3%); ELV's Wednesday print is the next read on cost trend. Still 13% below the $461.62 July high.
positions.driver: Post-earnings drift in the managed-care leader.

positions.name: Eli Lilly
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $1,257.03, +6.6% on the week (from $1,179.27), and within 3% of its $1,292.65 August all-time high after two big up days (Wed +3.6%, Thu +3.5% to a $1,275.88 high) on ~1.5x volume. Defensive-growth rotation target as money left semis and AI infrastructure (SOX fell 8 straight days, matching its longest losing streak since 2006).
positions.risks: No company-specific catalyst confirmed in news flow this week, so this is a relative-strength pick; Q3 earnings ~10/29-30 are outside the window. 43x earnings; a GLP-1 pricing headline can move it 5%+.
positions.driver: Highest-quality large-cap growth name making new relative highs as tech breaks.

positions.name: Walmart
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $118.81, +6.7% on the week (from $111.35) and 8 higher closes in the last 9 sessions; Thursday it gapped to a $121.38 high on 32M shares (1.6x average). Staples were among the sector leaders as the market rotated defensive; the 10-year fell ~15 bp on the week (best Treasury week since February), which helps premium-multiple defensives.
positions.risks: 43x earnings - priced as a growth stock; Thursday's gap partly faded. Still 12% below the $135.16 May high. Q3 report is mid-November, outside the window.
positions.driver: Defensive mega-cap with a clean uptrend and rising volume.

positions.name: Travelers
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $389.54, +5.6% on the week and at the high of the day after Friday's Q3 print: core EPS $9.18 vs $7.43 est. (+24% beat), net premiums written $12.41B vs $11.28B est., Bond & Specialty NWP +12%. The stock opened at $370 and closed +1.5% at $389.54 on 3.2M shares (2.4x average) - an outside reversal on a blowout beat. Fresh post-earnings drift into the week.
positions.risks: Personal Insurance premiums fell 7%; catastrophe losses rose to $538M. Within 2.5% of the $398.70 July high (resistance). CB reports Tue pm and can move P&C peers.
positions.driver: Blowout beat with a volume-confirmed close at the high - classic post-earnings momentum.

positions.name: NiSource
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $42.68, +3.5% on the day on 8.8M shares (1.8x average) and +4.7% on the week, after signing a new long-term energy agreement with Microsoft for its northwest Indiana data-center campus (raises expected NIPSCO customer savings to ~$1.75B). Utilities (XLU) were among Friday's leaders as Treasury yields held their pullback; NI bounced 11% off its 10/1 52-week low ($38.42).
positions.risks: Still 13% below the $49.21 June high. Q3 earnings late October/early November are outside the window. A yield rebound would hurt the group.
positions.driver: Fresh hyperscaler contract on 1.8x volume - the AI-power theme without the tech beta.

positions.name: Southern Company
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/16 at $91.18, +5.8% on the week (from $86.17) and 9 higher closes in the last 11 sessions, off its 9/29 52-week low ($81.69). Friday it rose 2.2% on 8.3M shares (1.35x average). Beneficiary of the 15 bp drop in the 10-year (to 5.10%) and of the AI-load story in the Southeast (Georgia Power data-center demand).
positions.risks: Rate-sensitive: if yields rebound the move reverses. Q3 earnings ~10/30 are outside the window. Pairs with NI, so utilities are 13% of the book.
positions.driver: Low-beta trend name to balance the energy and defense bets.
